subject: Pricing exhibit — clarification on packaging ladder / floor exceptions (redlines attached)
messages:
From: Sara Wong <sara.wong@brighthealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@brighthealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Question on pricing exhibit — mixed-package ladder and floor carveouts

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walk-through yesterday. Contracts flagged a potential ambiguity in Exhibit B (Order Schedule) around the packaging ladder and the application of minimum floors for mixed SKU bundles. Two quick items: 

1) The definition of "packaging ladder" in the schedule seems to apply the floor at the SKU level, but our procurement team expects it to apply at the bundle level when legacy SKUs are combined. Can you confirm the commercial intent?

2) Section 3.2(c) includes a "floor exception" for promotional re-rates but doesn't state whether promotional credits count toward the monthly minimum for the stability collar. BrightHealth requires clarity here for our internal sign-off.

I've attached a marked-up spreadsheet that highlights the lines where our pricing ops are seeing variance. We're close on economics but need the legal language tightened. Is your team able to provide a redline and a short note on operational effect (how true-ups would run)?

Ideally we can get this resolved before our procurement committee meets next Friday.

Thanks,
Sara Wong
Senior Sourcing Manager, BrightHealth

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Wong <sara.wong@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:02:41 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on pricing exhibit — mixed-package ladder and floor carveouts

Sara — thanks for the clear note and the spreadsheet. We're aligned that this is a clarification rather than a commercial concession. Quick answers up front: 

- Intent: the floor is intended to apply at the bundle (order schedule) level when legacy SKUs are intentionally migrated into a single package during onboarding or a migration promotion.
- Promotional credits: they are excluded from the monthly minimum calculation for the stability collar (we treat them as temporary adjustments, not recurring committed usage).

I'll loop in Karthik to validate the operational implications for true-ups and runbook changes; Marissa will help keep the commercial team in the loop. We'll circulate a redline (legal language + short ops notes) by EOD Friday.

Attaching the spreadsheet you sent to our thread so legal can track the exact line items.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts — Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0143

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Fwd: pricing exhibit clarification — can legal propose tight text?

Kim / Karthik — forwarding Sara's note. Two asks for legal:

- Provide a concise redline for Exhibit B that: (a) explicitly states "bundle-level application" when SKUs are intentionally combined; and (b) defines "promotional credit" and states it is excluded from monthly minimum calculations for the stability collar.
- Add a one-paragraph operational note explaining how monthly true-ups would compute (order of operations: usage measurement -> apply credits -> compare to floor -> compute true-up).

Laura — can you propose language that is tight (one-sentence fix + a short ops note) so we don't drag procurement? Karthik, please call out any commercial risk with that approach.

Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Wong <sara.wong@brighthealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: pricing exhibit — redline and operational note attached

Sara / team — please see the attached redline and an ops summary. Key points: 

1) Proposed redline (Exhibit B, Section 1(a)): 
"For the avoidance of doubt, where two or more legacy SKUs are intentionally combined by mutual written agreement into a single packaged offering (a 'bundle'), the floor and ceiling calculations in this Order Schedule shall be applied at the bundle level for the period during which the bundle is in effect."

2) Promotional credits (Section 3.2(c)) — proposed clarifying sentence: 
'Promotional credits' means one-time or time-limited credits issued in connection with a migration or limited-term commercial promotion and shall be excluded from the calculation of the Monthly Minimum for purposes of the Stability Collar in this Order Schedule.

3) Ops note (summary):
- Measurement window: calendar month.
- Step 1: aggregate billed usage per bundle.
- Step 2: subtract any promotional credits (as defined).
- Step 3: compare net usage to the Monthly Minimum; if below, compute true-up as (Monthly Minimum - net usage) * applicable per-unit rate.

Karthik — we avoided changing economics; it's purely definitional. If BrightHealth wants an economic concession (e.g., a lower floor for migrated bundles for the first 3 months), we can propose a limited promotional waiver instead.

Sara — attaching: BrightHealth_Pricing_Redline_v1.xlsx (tracked changes) and Order_Schedule_BH_SOW_v2.pdf (clean copy with redline comments in the margins). Also shared the DocuSign envelope for the order schedule if these edits are acceptable: https://www.docusign.com/en/brighthealth/order-schedule-signature

If that looks good, can we get confirmation before your procurement committee meeting next Friday? Happy to hop on a 15-minute call to walk the language.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference
